tweets.text: I would change my mind if a big network added privacy by default late and most people on it adopted it within a few years. For Bitcoin, I watch which arguments never end. What founding rule has your group fought over longest?

tweets.author: thejohnnycrypto.bsky.social
tweets.text: Bitcoin is a set of rules thousands of computers agree to follow. Anyone can run one of those computers (a node) at home, and anyone can plug in a miner. Both doors were open on day one. My view: the properties a network starts with are the ones it can defend later.
